use_of_force_authorities.core_rule: Prohibits the threat or use of force against territorial integrity or political independence
Preserves inherent right of individual or collective self-defense if an armed attack occurs
Security Council may authorize enforcement action
Connects force, non-intervention, self-determination, and territorial integrity
Lists acts that may qualify as aggression
Separates use of force, armed attack, and intervention
Emphasizes evidentiary burden, necessity, and proportionality
Addresses unlawful force, occupation, and responsibility

exceptions_framework.required_showing: Armed attack on victim state and request for assistance

exceptions_framework.legal_status: Potentially lawful outside Article 2(4) if valid
exceptions_framework.required_showing: Valid consent from competent government within lawful limits
exceptions_framework.main_risk: Coerced, contested, or ultra vires consent

exceptions_framework.required_showing: Claimed necessity to prevent mass atrocity
exceptions_framework.main_risk: Undermines Charter if used as unilateral license

exceptions_framework.required_showing: Armed attack attribution/unwilling-unable arguments, necessity, proportionality
